# brainTrade Work Log

## 2026-08-20 06:09 UTC — [Pillar 2] Calibrated entry-price bands fail terminal-payoff test

**Task:** Test a genuinely different Smart Entry risk-control hypothesis by freezing five non-overlapping entry-price bands and scoring the 2,649-row immutable YES forward ledger on terminal returns after a 2% stake cost deduction, including date robustness and recent-forward diagnostics.
**Finding:** Every full-ledger band was negative after costs. The 0.20–0.35 band returned -9.26% across 161 rows; 0.35–0.45 returned -17.92% across 181; 0.45–0.55 returned -21.80% across 2,001; 0.55–0.65 returned -10.30% across 123; and 0.65–0.80 returned -7.32% across 98. All five SolSt1ne reliability x edge scores were negative (-2.36% to -8.81%). The highest band achieved 68.37% WR but was profitable on only 8/17 dates and still had a -102% worst date. Since Aug 17, three bands appeared positive, but samples were only 14–31 rows across two to four dates; 0.35–0.45 swung from -46.79% to +56.67% by date, 0.55–0.65 lost on two of four dates, and 0.65–0.80 covered only two dates.
**My thinking:** Higher entry prices improve hit rate and median payoff, but not expectancy: paying more for apparent certainty leaves insufficient upside to absorb full-loss outcomes. The recent positive slices are exactly the kind of small, regime-local result that the earlier challengers showed can disappear at the binding checkpoint. Price calibration alone is therefore not a viable Smart Entry rule.
**Decision:** Set `P2_LEDGER2649_FIXED_PRICE_BANDS_COST2PCT / BAND20_35_N161_WR25.47_AVG_NEG9.26_SOL_NEG2.36_POSDATES4_OF20 / BAND35_45_N181_WR33.70_AVG_NEG17.92_SOL_NEG6.04_POSDATES5_OF18 / BAND45_55_N2001_WR40.43_AVG_NEG21.80_SOL_NEG8.81_POSDATES1_OF21 / BAND55_65_N123_WR55.28_AVG_NEG10.30_SOL_NEG5.69_POSDATES5_OF19 / BAND65_80_N98_WR68.37_AVG_NEG7.32_SOL_NEG5.01_POSDATES8_OF17 / RECENT_POSITIVE_SLICES_N14_TO31_ONLY_DATE_FRAGILE / ENTRY_PRICE_ALONE_REJECTED / NO_PROMOTION_NO_LIVE_CONFIG_CHANGE`.
**Next:** Preserve these frozen bands only as interaction labels. A future challenger must add an orthogonal risk-control signal, use a fresh cutoff, and pass at least 50 settlements across five dates with positive cost-adjusted mean, median, SolSt1ne score, and worst leave-one-date-out mean.

## 2026-08-20 05:59 UTC — [Pillar 1] Dominant BTC long scales while breadth slips

**Task:** Run a fresh top-20 Hyperliquid copy-intelligence scan and test whether the matched BTC cohort preserved the prior bullish reconstruction, with special attention to source breadth, flips, and concentration.
**Finding:** The scan completed 20/20 with zero failures. BTC changed from 5L/1S and +$32.726M net to 4L/2S and +$36.896M net, a +$4.170M signed improvement entirely within the same six matched BTC sources. Anon-0xecb6 added $4.814M (+14.75%) to a $37.450M long, more than explaining the aggregate improvement. Anon-0xf5d8 added $71.0K (+17.70%) to $472.0K and anon-0xfc66 held its $96.3K post-flip lo
